task.description: RE-GATE (rework_count 1) of WF-02 Step 1b for REQ-383 after CODE-DESIGNER's targeted rework of design doc sections 3.3 and 3.4, which were the sole BLOCKER findings in the prior gate (handoffs/WF02-REQ383-20260923/step-01b-code-design-validator.json, check 2e -- implementation code present). acceptance_criteria: a tenant admin can submit a new brand_colors.primary value through the screen, it round-trips through REQ-382's endpoint, and a confirmation is shown, matching EO-001's positive half

submitting a contrast-refused colour shows that endpoint's plain-language message on screen and the previously-applied colour remains visibly in effect -- no raw validation-error blob, matching EO-003
a regression test confirms StatusBadge's approved/waiting/failed colours are unchanged after a tenant colour change -- matching EO-002
the screen's own form has no field/control/code path capable of submitting a key this requirement did not itself add -- stated and verified explicitly

the stale NOTE (ISS-0527) is removed from tenant-branding-applied.yaml and web/tests/e2e/pipelines/tenant-branding.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts exists, passes against the real screen, and includes a first-paint-vs-settled-frame screenshot pair documenting EO-005's known flash

result.summary: Independently re-read lib/letflow/design/req383-appearance-settings-screen.md in full after CODE-DESIGNER's rework2 targeting §3.3 and §3.4 (the only two BLOCKER findings from the prior gate). §3.3: tenantSettingsApi.patchBrandColorPrimary is now a `@spec`-style signature (`@spec tenantSettingsApi.patchBrandColorPrimary(primary: string): Promise<TenantSettingsPatchResponse>`) followed by `//`-commented prose describing the request body shape and endpoint/verb -- no executable arrow-function body, no literal `client.patch(...)` call. This matches the pattern already accepted at §3.1 (readCurrentAppliedPrimary) in the prior gate. §3.4: the useMutation block is now a `@spec`-style signature (`@spec useMutation<TenantSettingsPatchResponse, ApiError, string>({ mutationFn, onSuccess, onError }): UseMutationResult`) plus two prose bullet lists ('State transitions on success' / 'State transitions on failure') stating each outcome's effects in prose -- no `onSuccess:`/`onError:` callback bodies, no ternary/control-flow code, no toast call as executable code. Ran a targeted grep for `=>`, `client.patch(`/`client.post(`/`client.get(`/`client.put(`, `useMutation({`, `onSuccess:`, `onError:` across the entire document: the only hits are the four pre-existing, unchanged §8 e2e `test.describe`/`test(...)` skeleton lines, whose bodies are exclusively `//`-commented step descriptions (no real Playwright API calls) -- these were already present and already passed in the prior gate, confirming no implementation code leaked in elsewhere as a side effect of the §3.3/§3.4 edit. Re-checked the AC1-AC5 -> design-element map at §11 (lines 607-615, unchanged verbatim from the previously-passed version): each of the 5 acceptance criteria still maps to the same concrete design elements (§2/§3.3/§3.4/§8-test1 for AC1; §0/§3.4/§4/§8-test2 for AC2; §6 for AC3; §5 for AC4; §7/§8-test3 for AC5). §10 cross-module dependencies and §9 open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4) are unchanged from the previously-reviewed version. Per this task's scope, did not re-verify the err.details.detail vs err.message claim against tenant_settings.ex/error.ex/client.ts -- that was independently confirmed correct against real merged source in the prior gate and is untouched by this rework. No TBD/deferral language found. No new implementation code found anywhere in the document. Gate PASSES.
